title: IELTS Academic 20 - Listening Test 4 - Part 1
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 1

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

00:53ANNOUNCER: Part 1. You will hear a man asking a friend for advice on things to do in the city with a family of visitors.
01:01ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6.
01:35ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 6.
01:42MAN: Sandra, I seem to remember you had some family visitors staying with you recently.
01:48WOMAN: Yeah, that's right. My brother and his family were here a couple of months ago.
01:54MAN: Well, I wanted to ask your advice. I've got my cousin and her family visiting next month, and as I don't have kids, I've no idea where to take them.
02:05WOMAN: Right. What about accommodation? Are they going to stay with you in your flat?
02:09MAN: No, thankfully. There wouldn't be room. My cousin wants me to recommend a hotel. Do you know anywhere?
02:16WOMAN: Yes, I do, actually. I always recommend people stay at the King's Hotel.
02:22MAN: Where's that near?
02:23WOMAN: It's about five minutes walk from Murray Station, so nice and central. It's actually on George Street.
02:32MAN: I think they're on quite a tight budget, so how much roughly is it to stay there?
02:37WOMAN: If you book a family room, it's about £125 per night. My brother paid for two double rooms in the end, and I think that was around £95 for each room.
02:51WOMAN: So how old are your cousin's kids?
02:53MAN: Twelve and nine. So I want to organise some trips while they're here. I was thinking of doing a bus tour of the city centre as none of them have been here before.
03:05WOMAN: Those bus tours are quite expensive. I think it's better to do a walking tour. It gives you a much better feel for the city. There's one that starts from Carlton Square. It takes a couple of hours and doesn't cost that much.
03:21WOMAN: If the weather's nice, one thing you could do is visit the old fort. You could get there by boat. The whole trip takes half a day.
03:29MAN: That's a really good idea. And if the weather's bad, I was thinking they could go to the Science Museum. But maybe they could do that when I'm at work.
03:41WOMAN: Yeah, don't forget. It's closed on Mondays.
03:44MAN: They're here from Saturday for four nights, so Tuesday would be best, I think. And it won't be so crowded then. Saturdays are terrible.
04:05WOMAN: There's another one starting soon on Space, which looks really good too.
04:15ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10.
04:41ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 7 to 10.
04:48WOMAN: Have you thought about where to take them to eat?
04:51MAN: Well, I really like all the food stalls at Clacton Market. My cousin's vegetarian. I know it's one of the best places for that kind of food.
05:05WOMAN: Definitely, and there'll be loads of choice for the kids too. You need to get there quite early though. At the weekend, most of the stalls stop serving lunch at 2.30.
05:15MAN: My cousin said she'd love to take the kids to a show at the theatre, but tickets are so expensive.
05:22WOMAN: But you can get some good deals if you book online with bargaintickets.com for the following day. On some seats, there's a 75% discount.
05:35WOMAN: There are lots of things you can do for free as well. Well, check and see if it's the same weekend as the Roots Music Festival in Blakewell Gardens. And if you're in Blakewell Gardens, climb Telegraph Hill. You'll be able to look right down on the port. Everyone's always really impressed because it's so huge.
06:24ANNOUNCER: That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.
